newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says no delay to $200 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Israel says no delay to $200 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Israel's Finance Ministry and Bank Hapoalim denied a press report that plans to arrange a $200 million syndicated bank loan had been postponed due to the recent political unrest.
The Finance Ministry denied the report and said the loan was set to go ahead. Bank Hapoalim said the loan would be raised on time at the end of October.

Israel's daily Globes cited a report in Britain's International Financial Review saying an initiative to raise a $200 million loan through an international consortium of banks had temporarily been halted.
"In view of the violent political crisis in Israel last week, the raising of the money through the consortium of foreign banks has been postponed to an unknown date," the review was quoted as saying.

Hapoalim is heading a group of banks that will organise a consortium of foreign banks to lend $200 million to Israel. The group includes Natwest, BNP of France, Bayerische Landesbank of Germany & Dai Ichi Kangyo of Japan.

Clashes erupted between Israelis and Palestinians last week after Israel opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. The death toll is now 73 people. A two-day White House summit held by President Bill Clinton to save the Middle East peace process ended Wednesday night with few concrete results.
